definitions.explanation: An attack or invasion by an outside force, historically referring to military incursions. Also used for natural disasters or phenomena that strike with force.

examples.japanese: {台風|たいふう}が{襲来|しゅうらい}した。
{敵|てき}の{襲来|しゅうらい}に{備|そな}えて{防備|ぼうび}を{固|かた}めた。
examples.english: They strengthened their defenses in preparation for an enemy attack.

examples.japanese: {元|げん}の{襲来|しゅうらい}は{日本|にほん}の{歴史|れきし}における{重要|じゅうよう}な{出来事|できごと}の{一|ひと}つだ。
examples.english: The Mongol invasions are one of the important events in Japanese history.

notes:
USAGE:
{襲来|しゅうらい} implies something coming at you with force from outside. It is commonly used for natural disasters ({台風|たいふう}の{襲来|しゅうらい}, {寒波|かんぱ}の{襲来|しゅうらい}) and historical military invasions. The word carries a dramatic, forceful tone. Historically, {元寇|げんこう} (the Mongol invasions of Japan) are often described using this word.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {台風|たいふう}の{襲来|しゅうらい}: a typhoon striking
- {敵|てき}の{襲来|しゅうらい}: enemy attack/invasion
- {寒波|かんぱ}の{襲来|しゅうらい}: onset of a cold wave
- {襲来|しゅうらい}に{備|そな}える: to prepare for an onslaught
